scorecard.rationale: The paper-filtered coffee crossover gives a favorable acute mental-fatigue result after pretest abstinence, with only partial masking. A fortified decaf post-nap comparison supports a similar acute direction. Driving and usual-diet exercise comparisons were inconclusive. Controlled capsule studies report more fatigue after short abrupt restriction and a tiredness benefit after abstention. The 2009 normal-use comparison did not establish the same tiredness response. The 1997 Lane reports and the 2015 intake and intervention records have shared or unresolved lineage. Manualized reduction trials measured total intake or pooled symptoms and did not isolate fatigue. A public account describes delayed fatigue followed by improved restfulness. The weight of evidence leaves minimal easing based on the beverage result, with the size and durability of any effect without withdrawal and in Parkinson disease open. The 39-person soluble-coffee crossover favored caffeinated soluble coffee in exploratory acute comparisons. Enriched versus regular soluble decaf was inconclusive. An additional coffeeberry crossover reported more mental fatigue after 100 mg extract at 60 minutes, with the primary 120-minute and 300 mg comparisons inconclusive. This unroasted fruit product is distant from brewed coffee. It raises uncertainty around general constituent transfer and leaves the limited sign from the beverage unchanged. A separate mechanistic review describes coffee-associated caffeic and chlorogenic acids and their isolated effects in protein-kinase signaling. It gives no independent brewed-coffee or fatigue outcome. The 12-person older-adult caffeine crossover reports higher vigor but an inconclusive fatigue subscale and exertion comparison. A later older-adult performance study measured timed tasks and readiness to invest effort without a dedicated fatigue comparison. The age-stratified mouse study measured isolated muscle power. A separate mouse soleus report gives opposite endurance directions under maximal and submaximal activation, and an earlier recovery protocol gives an inconclusive power result at its lower caffeine concentration. These findings constrain constituent extrapolation. The earlier beverage result remains the basis for the minimal easing lean. A historical museum interpretation attributes wakefulness during Sufi dhikr to brewed coffee. A separate osteoarthritis participant mentions coffee in a daily exercise and medication routine. Neither describes fatigue change. The secondary caffeine review describes withdrawal fatigue, an exposure and timing distinction. The applicable acute comparative beverage evidence still governs the minimal easing lean. The adenosine and xanthine reviews describe coffee, caffeine and cognition or alertness without independent fatigue results after brewed coffee. The older controlled beverage result remains the closest signed contrast. Additional adenosine and liver reviews confirm coffee-related exposures and mechanisms without a separate fatigue comparison. The controlled beverage evidence remains the basis for the easing lean. The caffeine and migraine review describes acute wakefulness and lower perceived fatigue, sleep interference and withdrawal headaches. The accounts do not provide a distinct brewed-coffee Parkinson fatigue contrast or change the direction from the controlled beverage evidence. The complete mouse original compares injected isolated caffeine with vehicle. Treadmill performance improved in animals with forebrain adenosine A2A receptor expression and the benefit was absent in the studied knockout comparisons. An injection and exercise endpoint do not identify a Parkinson subjective fatigue effect of brewed coffee. The controlled human beverage evidence remains the main directional basis. The coffee-bioactive review's citation to Cropley is the already-counted ACTRN12609001002279 family. The original's enriched-decaf contrast is inconclusive at p=.074. The sleep-bruxism exclusion and caffeine review have no independent coffee fatigue result. The Parkinson risk umbrella review reports coffee exposure and disease onset. The smell study used coffee as one screening odor. Neither provides a separate brewed-coffee treatment and chronic Parkinson fatigue result. Habitual coffee drinkers received isolated caffeine or hydrogen-rich drinks after sleep deprivation. The VAS alertness interaction was p=.095 and task results were separate. The study gives no brewed coffee or chronic Parkinson fatigue estimate. The sleep-wake review separates acute caffeine after abstinence, repeated dosing and conditions with limited sleep. Subjective sleepiness is a distinct outcome from clinical fatigue. Brewed coffee and Parkinson fatigue were not compared by the review. The prior direction is based on closer evidence. The stimulation and genetics papers concern caffeine as a confound and liability to decaf preference. Neither supplies a brewed coffee and Parkinson fatigue result. The linked 2022 chronic fatigue editorial remains at title and access depth. The Philippines community survey records two confirmed cases with fatigue and one coffee user, without a fatigue contrast by exposure. The earlier clinical fatigue cohort contains no coffee measure. Three additional public discussions report perceived benefit and no relief in different settings, with fatigue, sleepiness, drink preparation and medication timing incompletely distinguished. The closest brewed-coffee evidence and contrary observations retain the existing weak easing lean. The 2022 editorial original remains unavailable. The sleep-laboratory results concern bruxism, the Sister Study separates coffee and diagnostic risk from fatigue surveillance, and the solvent review mentions historical processing. None supplies a coffee-specific Parkinson fatigue contrast. The older editorial remains open at title and index depth. The primary-care panic group study reports caffeine and chronic fatigue diagnoses separately. The vestibular trial gives coffee advice without an independent coffee comparison. Neither updates the evidence on brewed coffee and Parkinson fatigue.
